subject: general
question: In a ∆ABC, the internal bisectors of the angle B and the angle C intersect at an angle of 105°. What is the value of the angle A?
solution:
**Given:**

The internal bisectors of angle B and angle C intersect at an angle of 105°

**Formula Used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73f7901c6fb7e025de592ea58e1227f7ba5bad0d4e5d165aca95d4319eed613e.png] 

In an △ABC, if internal bisectors of angles B and C are joined at D, then

⇒ ∠BDC = 90° + ∠BAC/2

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/54f5fc4592063df78ba73c0de395c02e903e614eb26754ceeecfa342c69e3300.png] 

∠BOC = 105°

Internal bisectors of angles B and C are joined at O

∠BDC = 90° + ∠BAC/2

⇒ 105° = 90° + ∠BAC/2

⇒ 105° - 90° = ∠BAC/2

⇒ 15° = ∠BAC/2

⇒ ∠BAC = 30°

**∴ The value of angle A is 30°.**
